exceptions.reason: Today's core's Codex translator sends empty instructions on every Responses request; the extension sends the request's instructions as the client wrote them.

Today's core's Codex translator adds this default to every Responses request with tools (tool_choice, parallel_tool_calls, strict false, additionalProperties false); the extension sends the client's tools and choices as the client wrote them.
Today's core derives a session ID per conversation and sends it as prompt_cache_key; the extension has no session identity to derive from, so it sends only the client's own prompt_cache_key.
Today's core sends its session ID as the x-grok-conv-id header; the extension sends the header only when the client's body carries a prompt_cache_key, since it has no session identity of its own.
The xAI extension names itself in its User-Agent (pluxy-xai and its version) and does not copy the Grok CLI's identity; today's core sends the Grok workspace's User-Agent unless the client sent one.
A non-streamed client gets a non-streamed upstream request, and its reply is read as one response; today's core always asks xAI for a stream and reads the stream into one reply.
Follows the request's stream flag (see the upstream stream exception); today's core always asks for an event stream.

The extension sends every custom tool the client declares as a function with one input string, because a client cannot run a function call for a tool it declared custom (the Codex CLI ends the turn with an incompatible payload error). The description tells xAI to put the tool's text in input and carries the grammar that the format field held. Today's core sends the client's description unchanged and gives a custom tool other than apply_patch no input field.

Today's core sends an empty-object schema for a custom tool other than apply_patch.

The one response lists the call as a custom_tool_call with the input text, where today's core lists a function_call with JSON arguments. A client cannot run a function call for a tool it declared custom (the Codex CLI ends the turn with an incompatible payload error), so the extension returns xAI's call to a custom tool as a custom_tool_call with the call's text as its input. Today's core does this for apply_patch only and returns a function_call for any other custom tool.
